problem: Existing agent benchmarks abstract away body motion (scripted or simulator-defined actions), while end-to-end VLAs entangle the decision with a learned motor policy, and humanoids can fail from balance loss. So it is unclear how far a frozen generalist VLM's reasoning extends into closed-loop whole-body physical action.
motivation: The paper wants to measure 'action intelligence', the ability to decide what a body should do next at sub-second rate, with the decision decoupled from motor control while the body still acts under contact, collision and gravity. This allows each failure to be attributed to the decision maker rather than to balance or motor tracking.
key_idea: Let a frozen off-the-shelf VLM pick atomic parameterized whole-body skills each 0.5 s, realized by a skill-ControlNet motion generator and executed in a half-physics simulator (contact/gravity, no balance failure), then benchmark this with find-navigate-sit episodes.
insight: Perception is not the bottleneck: GeoFindSR vs FindSR differ by only 5-10 points for top models. Failures concentrate in embodied self-awareness: 34% of nav failures are body-awareness errors and 30% are stop-while-far distance hallucination, and 81% of interaction failures are body-placement errors (58% sit on thin air). Ablations show the verifier (NavSR 27.0 to 2.0) and the mid-level objective (InteractSR 18.9 to 0.0) matter most, while longer text history saturates and 10 image frames hurt (NavSR 13.0).
method: Harnessed VLM decision module: at each step it gets the prompt, egocentric RGB and compact text history, outputs an explicit ego-perception state, then reasons high-to-mid-to-low, and emits a JSON skill call <s_t, c_t>.
Atomic skill vocabulary: walk(x,z,psi), side_step, step_back, turn_in_place, climb_upstairs, walk_downstairs, sit_in_place(h), stop; composition is left to the VLM.

Skill-specific spatial verifier: a short-context, skill-triggered checklist re-answered from the current view; it accepts a proposal or replaces it with a corrected skill (e.g., checks arrival before stop, seat behind body before sit).

Motion Base DiT: 38M-parameter, 10-layer flow-matching DiT trained on AMASS. It takes 5 history frames as tokens and predicts the next 15 frames (0.5 s at 30 fps), skill-agnostic, with a 30-step midpoint solver.
Plug-and-play skill ControlNets: one zero-init ControlNet adapter per skill on the frozen base, with parameters read from curated clip geometry, so new skills are added without retraining others.

Half-physics simulator: Habitat + Bullet at 120 Hz; the generated poses are converted to equivalent joint velocities driving a passive body (stiffness 1.0), giving collision, gravity and movable-object effects without balance failure.

HumanCLAW-Bench: 1,218 find-navigate-interact(sit) episodes in 41 HSSD val houses across 6 categories, with progressive FindSR/NavSR/InteractSR requiring both objective and acknowledged success, plus collision, disturbance, jerk and token-cost metrics.

setting.backbone: Frozen off-the-shelf VLMs (GPT-5.5, Gemini-3.1, Gemini-2.5, Claude-4.8, Gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-27B, InternVL3.5-38B) as decision maker; separately trained motion DiT + ControlNets
setting.model_size: Motion DiT 38M; VLMs 27B-38B for open ones
setting.training_data: Decision VLM: none (frozen, zero-shot). Motion generator: AMASS/BABEL clips, manually filtered per skill, adapters trained 0.5M-1.5M steps.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (512x512) + text history; no proprioception or contact signal
setting.action_space: 8 atomic parameterized whole-body skills executed as 0.5 s, 15-frame humanoid motion chunks
setting.simulator: Habitat with Bullet physics (half-physics), HSSD scenes
setting.privileged: none for the agent (GT semantics/geometry used only for evaluation and root-cause labeling)

results: No VLM solves the benchmark: the best, Gemini-3.1, reaches FindSR 64.9 / NavSR 42.4 / InteractSR 16.8, with Gemma-4-31B (58.1/28.7/11.1) the best open model. The skill controller is reliable, with achievement ratios of about 0.97-1.00 for walk/turn/side-step/step-back/sit versus MoMask's ratios that deviate from 1 with far larger variance.
limitations: Small interaction vocabulary (only sit) and skill granularity that defines where the decision failure is attributed
Half-physics removes balance and motor control, so sim-to-real humanoid transfer is untested
Agent has no proprioceptive or contact signal, which may confound the body-awareness findings; no comparison with trained action policies
